regime.label: Hot
regime.reading: Housing costs more and is competed for harder than is usual in this city, and has not yet turned.

housing_pressure.label: Housing pressure
housing_pressure.question: Is demand outrunning the housing available?

distress.label: Distress
distress.question: Is an orderly slowdown turning into financial stress?

signatures.label: Overheating
signatures.summary: The boom's second act: prices and short-term-rental supply keep climbing while the things that fund them stop. Transactions and permits roll over first, and the storefront churn rate rises before net closures do.

signatures.label: Boom
signatures.summary: People and money arriving faster than the city can house them. Rents and transactions rise together, business formation accelerates, and attention from outside the country runs ahead of the official population count.

signals_against.label: Non-Spanish share of city article views

signatures.label: Distress
signatures.summary: Jobs go first, then the storefronts, then the courts. Foreclosures, evictions and insolvencies rise together while hiring and business formation fall; hardship attention climbs before the judicial series, which are the slowest evidence we have.

signatures.label: Orderly cooling
signatures.summary: Heat leaving the market without anyone being forced. Prices and transactions decelerate while employment holds and the distress measures stay flat. This is the benign case, and it is worth being able to name it.

signatures.label: Tourism shock
signatures.summary: Visitor demand moves independently of the local economy. Flights, hotel nights and port arrivals turn together while employment and housing lag behind — a shock arriving from outside the city rather than inside it.

signals_against.label: Non-Spanish share of city article views

signatures.label: Regulatory shock
signatures.summary: Short-term-rental supply contracts while visitor demand does not. Listings and licensed tourist dwellings fall together with hotel demand steady or rising — the fingerprint of a rule change rather than a demand change.

supply.label: Dwelling stock
supply.plain: How many homes exist in total.
supply.note: Published by province only — there is no municipal breakdown in the ministry's estimate. Madrid province holds about 3.05 million dwellings against roughly 1.5 million in the municipality, so this is provincial context rather than a count of homes in the city. Per-dwelling ratios built on it inherit that scope and are labelled accordingly.

source.publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda y Agenda Urbana

supply.label: Housing completions

supply.label: Housing starts

source.publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda y Agenda Urbana

supply.label: Urban land price
supply.plain: What building land costs per square metre. It moves before construction does.

source.publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda y Agenda Urbana

credit.label: Doubtful loan ratio
credit.plain: What share of bank loans are not being repaid. Rises late, after trouble has already happened.

credit.label: Euribor 12-month
credit.plain: The interest rate most Spanish variable-rate mortgages are priced off. When this rises, monthly repayments follow.
credit.suspect_note: The latest release sits 5.1 median absolute deviations from this measure's recent normal. Treated as provisional — publishers commonly release a partial period first — and kept off the front page until a later release confirms it.

credit.label: New mortgage rate

credit.label: New mortgages on dwellings
credit.plain: How many new mortgages were signed on homes.

work.label: Job postings index
work.plain: Index level of total job postings on Indeed for Spain (100 = February 2020), seasonally adjusted and 7-day lagged. A forward-looking indicator of hiring intent.
work.note: Indeed publishes daily observations for both 'total postings' and 'new postings'; we use 'total postings'. The index is seasonally adjusted. February 2020 baseline = 100. Recent months are withheld until Indeed's data is complete (before the month ends).

source.license: Free for public use with attribution

work.label: New contracts registered
work.plain: How many new employment contracts were registered. Hiring shows up here first.

work.label: New vehicle registrations
work.plain: How many vehicles were newly registered — a fast, keyless read on household and business confidence.
work.note: Not "new cars sold". Counts DGT transaction code 1 ("Matriculación ordinaria y de ciclomotores") only — genuine new registrations, never transfers of ownership, temporary plates, re-registrations or de-registrations, which are separate transaction codes and excluded. But that transaction code spans nearly every vehicle class, not cars alone: in a sampled month, passenger cars were about 69% of qualifying rows, motorcycles and mopeds about 14%, vans about 9%, and the remainder trucks, buses, trailers, agricultural machinery and a handful of historic and special vehicles. The province is where the registration was filed (DGT's own COD_PROVINCIA_MAT), not the vehicle owner's home province (COD_PROVINCIA_MAT and COD_PROVINCIA_VEH are different fields in the source file) — Madrid runs 3-4x above Barcelona because national fleet, leasing and rental-car operators file their registrations there administratively regardless of where the vehicle will actually operate. That is a real, widely-reported feature of Spanish registration statistics, not a data error: this adapter's province-level annual totals were cross-checked against DGT's own published "Matriculación por provincias" table and matched to within the one month DGT itself never published.

work.label: Registered unemployment
work.plain: How many people are signed on as unemployed at the job office.

tourism.label: Airport flights (daily traffic)
tourism.plain: How many flights the airport handled. Counted daily, so it arrives weeks before passenger figures.

tourism.plain: Room revenue per available room — price and occupancy combined, so it falls if either does.

str.plain: What share of Airbnb listings are whole homes rather than a spare room — whole homes are the ones taken off the long-term market.

distress.label: Companies dissolved
distress.plain: How many companies were wound up.

distress.label: Companies incorporated
distress.plain: How many new companies were registered.

distress.label: Evictions carried out
distress.plain: How many evictions courts actually carried out.
distress.note: Evictions actually carried out, which is the sum of the mortgage, rental-law and other categories CGPJ publishes. It moves separately from eviction orders received, because each court district works through its own enforcement backlog: in the first quarter of 2026, orders received rose sharply almost everywhere while executions fell in Zaragoza and the Balearics and rose in Madrid and Bizkaia. The most recent quarter is provisional and is usually revised upward, so treat it as incomplete rather than as a turning point.
distress.suspect_note: Every city moved sharply the same way in this release, which is far more often a partial period, a definition change or a parsing error than a simultaneous national event. Treated as provisional and kept off the front page until a later release confirms it.

distress.label: Insolvency proceedings
distress.plain: How many businesses formally went insolvent.

distress.label: Mortgage foreclosures filed
distress.plain: How many times a lender started court proceedings to take a home over unpaid mortgage debt.

attention.label: City attention share
attention.plain: How much of Wikipedia's traffic goes to this city, so years can be compared as reading habits change.
attention.note: City article views per million views of the same language editions. Raw pageview counts fell about 45% between 2021 and 2026 as search behaviour changed, so only the share is comparable across years.

attention.label: Hardship attention (Euribor, eviction, benefits)
attention.plain: How often people look up Euribor, evictions, mortgages and unemployment benefits. Worry, not hardship itself.

attention.label: Non-Spanish share of city article views
attention.plain: What share of the city's Wikipedia readers are reading in a language other than Spanish — a rough read on interest from abroad.

attention.label: Relocation attention (padrón, NIE, visas)
attention.plain: How often people look up residency registration, visas and foreigner ID — the paperwork of moving to Spain.
